mots.sens: This term refers to 'porters' or 'guards'. In the biblical context, the porters were responsible for watching over the entrance of the temple and protecting the holy places. Their role symbolizes spiritual vigilance and the protection of sacred things, highlighting the importance of holiness in worship. Theologically, this reminds us that every believer is called to watch over their own spiritual life and to protect the faith community.

This word refers to 'Korah', an ancestor of the lineage of the porters. Korah is associated with rebellion in the book of Numbers, but here, his legacy is redefined by the devoted service of his descendants. This illustrates how God can transform family history and use lineages for His glory. Spiritually, this teaches us that our past does not define our potential for service in the kingdom of God.

This name means 'God has made complete'. It evokes a notion of fullness and perfection in service. The fact that Meschélémia is a porter emphasizes that serving God involves total consecration and devotion. This reminds us that in our service, we must seek to be complete and whole before God.

mots.sens: This name means 'the one who is complete' or 'the one who is at peace'. It evokes the idea of fullness and divine security. Every believer has a unique place and role in the divine plan, and we must live in awareness of our calling and God's faithfulness to us.

17.interpretation: This verse illustrates the necessity of organization in the service of God, showing that every member of the community has a role to play. It reminds us that service to God must be done with diligence and order.

As believers, we are called to be guardians of our faith and to serve zealously in our churches and communities, each according to their gifts and abilities.

mots.sens: This word means 'gate' or 'entrance'. It evokes not only the idea of a physical opening but also that of a place of passage and encounter. In the biblical context, gates are often symbols of protection and access to the community, also representing the presence of God in the lives of believers.

This term translates to 'way' or 'passage'. It designates a route of travel but can also symbolize the spiritual journey of an individual. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of the direction and path that God's servants must take in their ministry.

This word means 'extremity' or 'border'. It indicates a specific geographical position but can also be interpreted as a metaphor for the limits that God has established. Spiritually, this reminds us that God has a plan for every aspect of our lives, even at the extremities of our existence.

This word means 'face' or 'presence'. It is often used to refer to the face of God, symbolizing communion and intimacy with Him. In the context of this verse, it reminds us that our service must be directed toward the presence of God, seeking to please Him in all that we do.

18.epoque: This passage is set during the reign of David, a period marked by the establishment of the kingdom of Israel and the preparation of the temple. It is a time of reorganization and devotion to God, where worship takes a central place in the life of the people.
18.passage: In 1 Chronicles 26, the chapter deals with the organization of the gatekeepers and guardians of the temple, highlighting the importance of each function in the service of God. Verse 18 specifies the locations of the gatekeepers, illustrating the structure and divine order in worship.
18.culture: In Israelite culture, the gates of cities and temples were places of gathering and decision. The gatekeepers had a crucial role, not only for security but also for welcoming the faithful, which underscores the importance of community in worship.
18.interpretation: This verse teaches us that every aspect of service to God is important and that order is essential in worship. The gatekeepers, by their position, are guardians of holiness and access to the divine presence, reminding us of our responsibility to watch over our relationship with God.
18.commentaire: This passage encourages us to recognize our role in the faith community and to serve diligently. Like the gatekeepers, we are called to protect and welcome those who seek God, ensuring that every aspect of our service is done with integrity and devotion. By engaging in our ministry, we participate in God's work in the world.

mots.sens: This term refers to a 'guardian' or 'porter', and it is derived from the Hebrew root that evokes the idea of watching or overseeing. In the context of temple service, the porters had the responsibility of protecting access to the holy place, symbolizing the separation between the sacred and the profane. Spiritually, this reminds us of the importance of keeping our hearts and lives in accordance with the holiness of God.

This name designates one of the families of the Levites, descendants of Merari, who had specific functions in the service of the tabernacle. The name itself is related to 'bitter', which can evoke the challenges that this lineage may have encountered. Theologically, this emphasizes that even amidst trials, God uses individuals and families to fulfill His plan.

Korah is a biblical figure whose descendants, the Korahites, were called to serve in the temple. The name is often associated with rebellion, but here it reminds us that even those who have experienced failures can be restored and used by God. This teaches us that divine grace can transform stories of rebellion into stories of service and devotion.

This term means 'guard' or 'watch', and it is used to describe the responsibilities of the porters in the temple. The notion of 'mishmar' implies constant vigilance and a sacred responsibility. Spiritually, this calls us to be guardians of our faith, watching over our relationship with God and our commitment to His house.

19.epoque: This passage is set during the reign of David, when the people of Israel were organizing for worship and service at the temple. It is a period of restoration and centralization of worship in Jerusalem.
19.passage: 1 Chronicles 26 describes the organization of the porters and guardians of the temple, highlighting the importance of each role in worship. This chapter sheds light on the structure and order necessary to honor God in service.
19.culture: In Israelite culture, service at the temple was an honor and a sacred responsibility. The porters, in particular, had a crucial role in maintaining the holiness of the place of worship and in welcoming those who came to worship.
19.interpretation: This verse reminds us that every member of the community has an important role to play in worship and service to God. The porters, as guardians, symbolize the necessity of protecting and respecting the holy place while being attentive to the presence of God.
19.commentaire: The organization of the porters in the temple teaches us the importance of order and responsibility in our spiritual lives. As believers, we are called to be guardians of our faith, watching over our relationship with God and our commitment to our community. This encourages us to serve diligently and to honor the sacred in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This name means 'brother of Yahweh'. It evokes an intimate and sacred relationship with God, highlighting the role of the Levites as intermediaries between the people and the Lord. In the context of managing the treasures of the house of God, it reminds us that those who serve in God's affairs must have a deep spiritual connection with Him.

This term designates a person who is a citizen or a member of a community. In the context of managing the treasures, it underscores the importance of responsibility and the management of sacred goods, which belong to the community of faith. It reminds us that every member of the Church is called to actively participate in the life of the community and in the management of God's resources.

This word means 'treasure' or 'reserve'. It refers to valuable goods, often associated with holy things. Spiritually, this underscores the value of the gifts and resources that God has entrusted to His people, and the importance of managing them with wisdom and integrity.

This term means 'sacred' or 'holy'. It designates everything that is set apart for the service of God. In the context of this verse, it reminds us that the treasures of the house of God are not only material but also spiritual, and they must be treated with the utmost respect and profound reverence.

20.epoque: This passage is set during the reign of David, when the people of Israel were establishing their worship and religious structure around the Tabernacle and later the Temple.
20.passage: Chapter 26 of 1 Chronicles deals with the organization of the Levites and their responsibilities in the house of God. Achiyah is mentioned as a supervisor of the treasures, highlighting the importance of managing sacred resources.
20.culture: In Israelite culture, the Levites had a central role in worship and the management of religious affairs. The management of treasures was crucial for maintaining the purity and integrity of worship.
20.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that God expects us to be good stewards of what He has entrusted to us, whether material or spiritual resources. The management of God's treasures is a sacred responsibility that requires great integrity and a commitment to holiness.
20.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of responsibility in the service of God. As believers, we are called to wisely manage the resources that God has entrusted to us, ensuring that they are used for His glory and the good of the community. This prompts us to reflect on our own management of material and spiritual goods in our daily lives.

mots.sens: The name Laedan means 'one who is supported' or 'one who is strong'. It is associated with the lineage of the Gershonites, descendants of Levi, which underscores the importance of the priestly lineage and service in the tabernacle. The mention of Laedan here reminds us of God's faithfulness to His promises and the essential role of families in divine service.

The term 'Gershonite' derives from the Hebrew root 'גּוּר' which means 'to sojourn' or 'to dwell'. This evokes the idea of those who are called to live in the presence of God, serving in the tabernacle. Spiritually, this reminds us that we are called to dwell in the presence of God and to serve in our community of faith.

The word 'mishpachah' means 'family' or 'clan'. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of family structures in the service of God. It teaches us that every family member has a role to play in the divine plan and that the community of faith is strengthened by the commitment of each family.

21.epoque: This passage is set during the post-exilic period, when the Israelites were returning to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple and restore worship. It was a time of reorganization and redefinition of Israel's national and spiritual identity.
21.passage: In 1 Chronicles 26, the chapter deals with the organization of the porters and the temple officials. It highlights the importance of roles and responsibilities in worship, emphasizing that each family had a specific function in the service of the Lord.
21.culture: Israelite culture valued lineage and heritage, particularly concerning religious service. Families were responsible for passing on traditions and sacred duties, and each member played a crucial role in community life.
21.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God uses families and lineages to accomplish His purposes. The mention of Laedan and the Gershonites underscores the importance of continuity in service and faithfulness to the divine calling, even across generations.
21.commentaire: The example of Laedan and the Gershonites encourages us to recognize our place in God's plan. Every family and every individual has a unique role to play in the kingdom of God. As believers, we must commit to serving faithfully, supporting one another, and honoring our spiritual heritage.

mots.sens: This word designates God in all His power and majesty. It is often used to express divine sovereignty and God's role as creator and guardian of the universe. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the sacred responsibility of the guardians of the treasures of the house of the Lord, indicating that everything consecrated to God must be treated with the utmost respect and care.

This term means 'treasure' or 'storehouse', and it evokes the idea of precious wealth, often associated with spiritual or material resources. In the context of the house of the Lord, it refers to the sacred goods that must be protected. This reminds us that God's possessions, whether material or spiritual, must be managed with integrity and devotion.

This verb means 'to keep', 'to protect', or 'to watch over'. It implies an action of attentive surveillance and preservation. In the context of this verse, it underscores the importance of vigilance and responsibility in the service of God, calling us to be faithful guardians of what is holy.

22.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the post-exilic period, when the people of Israel were restoring their worship and religious institutions under the leadership of David and his successors.
22.passage: In 1 Chronicles 26, the chapter deals with the organization of the Levites and the gatekeepers, highlighting the importance of managing the sacred resources of the house of the Lord. This verse emphasizes the specific role of the sons of Jehiéli in this essential task.
22.culture: In Israelite culture, managing the treasures of the house of God was a sacred responsibility, involving not only material aspects but also spiritual ones. The treasures represented God's presence and provision among His people.
22.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that we are called to be guardians of the gifts and resources that God has entrusted to us. This includes not only our material possessions but also our talents, time, and commitment to serving God.
22.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of responsibility in the service of God. Just as Zetham and Joel guarded the treasures of the house of the Lord, we must watch over what God has entrusted to us, being faithful in our stewardship. This calls us to a life of devotion, where every aspect of our existence is dedicated to the glory of God.

mots.sens: Amram is a Hebrew name meaning 'exalted people'. He is the father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, and represents an important priestly lineage. The mention of the Amramites in this verse highlights the significance of Moses' descent in temple service, emphasizing the continuity of the priestly ministry and faithfulness to the divine covenant.

Jitsehar means 'light' or 'brilliant'. This name is associated with the lineage of Levi, emphasizing a role of service in worship. The Jitseharites, as descendants of Levi, are called to bring God's light to His people, which has a spiritual implication regarding each believer's responsibility to be a witness of divine light in the world.

Hébron means 'association' or 'communion'. It is a city of historical and spiritual significance for the Israelites. The Hebronites, as descendants of Levi, remind us of the importance of communion and unity in the service of God, emphasizing that ministry is a collective effort and that each member has a vital role to play.

Uziél means 'strength of God'. This name evokes divine power and protection. The Uziélites, descendants of Levi, are called to serve with the strength that God grants them, reminding believers that their strength for service comes from their relationship with God and their dependence on His power.

23.epoque: This passage is set during the time of the Israelite monarchy, after the conquest of the promised land, when David organized worship and service in the temple.
23.passage: In 1 Chronicles 26, the chapter deals with the organization of the gatekeepers and temple officials, highlighting the importance of the different Levitical lineages in the service of God.
23.culture: In Israelite culture, lineage and heritage were crucial, especially for religious functions. Each group had specific roles, which reinforced order and structure in worship.
23.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God has chosen specific families for service in His temple, illustrating how He orders and structures worship. Each lineage has a unique function, emphasizing the importance of diversity in the body of Christ.
23.commentaire: This passage teaches us that every believer has a place and function in God's plan. Just as the Amramites, Jitseharites, Hebronites, and Uziélites had specific roles, we are called to discover and exercise our gifts for the service of God and the edification of the Church. Let us be attentive to our calling and engaged in the mission entrusted to us.

mots.sens: This name means 'God is redemption'. It is derived from the root 'שׁוּב' which evokes return or restoration. In the context of this verse, it highlights divine providence in managing the resources of the temple, indicating that even in material affairs, God is involved and active.

This term means 'man' or 'individual'. It is often used in the Bible to designate a man of value or a leader. In this verse, it emphasizes the responsibility and role of a man chosen by God to manage the treasures, highlighting the importance of faithfulness in the tasks entrusted.

The mention of Schebuel as the steward of the treasures reminds us that the management of God's goods must be done with an awareness of the unity and holiness of the divine mission.

24.epoque: This verse is set during the post-exilic period, when the Israelites were restoring their worship and religious institutions under the leadership of David and Solomon.
24.passage: In 1 Chronicles 26, the chapter deals with the organization of the Levites and temple officials, highlighting the importance of management and responsibility in the worship of God.
24.culture: Israelite culture valued responsibility and integrity in managing resources, especially those consecrated to God. The treasures of the temple were considered sacred and required careful management.
24.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that God chooses individuals for specific roles in His work, and that every task, even those that seem material, has spiritual significance. The stewardship of treasures is a symbol of how we should manage our resources as faithful believers.
24.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of faithfulness and responsibility in our respective roles, whether in the church or in our personal lives. As believers, we are called to be good stewards of the resources that God entrusts to us, recognizing that everything belongs to Him and should be used for His glory.

mots.sens: The name Rechabia means 'Yahweh has enlarged'. This term is derived from the Hebrew root 'רָחַב' (rachab), which means 'to enlarge' or 'to extend'. In a spiritual sense, this can evoke the idea that God extends His blessings and promises through generations, emphasizing the importance of lineage and faithfulness in serving God.

In the context of this verse, it can symbolize the continuity of peace and prosperity in the priestly lineage, reminding us that God is the source of peace for His people.

25.epoque: This passage is set in the post-exilic period, when the Israelites were returning to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple and restore their worship. It is a time marked by restoration and the reorganization of religious functions within the Jewish community.

25.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of lineage and the transmission of spiritual responsibilities. Each generation has a role to play in God's plan, and this passage reminds us that we are called to be faithful witnesses of our spiritual heritage.
25.commentaire: This passage teaches us that our service to God is often rooted in a family and spiritual history. By recognizing our ancestors in faith, we are encouraged to continue their legacy by living faithfully and passing on the faith to future generations. Each name in this lineage represents a story of devotion and commitment to God, calling us to do the same in our own lives.

mots.sens: This name means 'peace' or 'one who brings peace'. 26.epoque: This passage is set during the reign of King David, a period marked by the unification of the tribes of Israel and the centralization of worship in Jerusalem.

26.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of responsibility in serving God. Just as Schelomith and his brothers guarded the holy treasures, we are called to guard our faith and protect our relationship with God. This involves constant vigilance and a commitment to live according to divine principles.

mots.sens: This term refers to the spoils or plunder taken during a war. It evokes not only material wealth but also victory and divine protection over the people of Israel. This verb means 'to consecrate' or 'to sanctify'. It implies an act of dedicating something to God, setting it apart for holy use. In the context of this verse, it underscores the idea that even material goods, when offered to God, acquire spiritual value, becoming instruments of service for the Lord.

27.epoque: This passage is set during the reign of David, when the people of Israel were establishing themselves firmly in the promised land and preparing for the construction of the temple.
27.passage: In 1 Chronicles 26, the chapter discusses the organization of the gatekeepers and temple officials, highlighting the importance of managing resources and service in the house of the Lord.

27.commentaire: This passage invites us to reflect on how we use our resources. Whether it be our time, money, or talents, we are called to dedicate them to God. By doing so, we participate in God's work and testify to our gratitude for His blessings in our lives.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to consecrate' or 'to set apart for sacred use.' It evokes the idea of dedicating something to God, marking a separation from the profane to the holy. Samuel, whose name means 'God has heard,' is a prophet and judge of Israel. He played a crucial role in establishing the monarchy in Israel and in the anointing of kings. His name here reminds us of divine authority in the consecration process and the importance of listening to God's voice.

28.epoque: This passage is set in the time of the Old Testament, during the reign of David, when the religious and political structures of Israel were being formed.

28.commentaire: This passage invites us to reflect on our own lives and what we have consecrated to God. Are we good guardians of our faith and commitment to Him? As believers, we are called to protect and honor what is holy in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This term refers to the descendants of Jitschar, one of the sons of Kehath, who was himself one of the sons of Levi. Spiritually, this reminds us that God chooses specific people for specific tasks in His work.

In a spiritual sense, this evokes the idea that God establishes authorities to maintain order and justice, thus reflecting His just character.

29.epoque: This passage is set during the reign of David, when the organization of worship and administration in Israel was in full development, following the conquest of the promised land.

30.epoque: This passage is set during the period of the establishment of the kingdom of Israel under David, when the tribes were organized for the service of worship and administration.

As believers, we are called to be 'mighty men and women,' ready to serve and watch over the affairs of the Lord in our daily lives. Let us cultivate a spirit of dedication and vigilance, actively engaging in our community and our church.

mots.sens: This term refers to the members of the tribe of Levi who are from the city of Hebron. In the context of this verse, it evokes the necessity of conducting inquiries and verifications to establish the legitimacy and responsibility of the tribe's members. 31.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of David, a pivotal period for Israel, marked by the unification of the tribes and the centralization of worship in Jerusalem.

As believers, we are called to be 'gibborim' in our faith, striving to serve with courage and dedication. mots.sens: This term means 'man' or 'male' and is often used to refer to an individual as a member of a community. This underscores the importance of spiritual and moral strength in serving God and the community.

32.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of King David, a period marked by the unification of the tribes of Israel and the consolidation of the kingdom under a single authority. It is a time of transition and strengthening of Israel's national and spiritual identity.

32.interpretation: This verse teaches us that God chooses courageous men and women to serve in His work. The mention of 'mighty men' emphasizes that serving God requires courage and determination, and that every leader must be ready to assume both spiritual and practical responsibilities.

As believers, we are called to be 'mighty men and women', ready to take on responsibilities in our families and churches.
